question.problem:
Calculate the value of 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14144360/assets/1fd9cafe0db4412b48885cebacd68b9866a79fadfdb7767c3b63f8469d31bfea.svg)

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{31}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.*
question.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{31}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(11-3) \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$
